title: Retention Storyline & Deck Kit — Core + Enterprise
content:
Purpose: concise deck kit and speaker notes that teams can adapt for two flavors of QBR: Core (SMB / mid-market) and Enterprise. Goal is to reduce prep time, improve signal-to-noise for renewals, and make risk/expansion calls consistent across AEs and CSMs. This is a working draft — intended to be copied into a slide template and trimmed to fit 30/45/60 minute customer slots.

How to use: copy the appropriate slide sequence, populate the metrics table with values pulled from the QBR numbers sheet, and align on 2–3 action items with owners and deadlines before the meeting ends.

Core (10-slide, 30min) flow and speaker notes:
1. Title + 1-line value recap (2 min)
   - Company logo, CSM + AE names, renewal window, ARR band, key product areas in use.
   - Speaker note: Start with one sentence of impact — e.g., "Over the last 90 days you've reduced inference cost per request by 22% after switching to batch profiling."

2. Agenda and desired outcomes (1 min)
   - What we will cover and what we want to leave with (decision on renewal, 1 pilot next quarter, or allocate additional seats).

3. Health snapshot (3 min)
   - Top-line health: usage delta, latency SLA compliance, support tickets open, infra incidents.
   - Speaker note: Call out anything that needs escalation. If red flags exist, surface them now.

4. Outcomes by team / use case (5 min)
   - Short bullets for three primary stakeholders (engineering, product, ops).
   - Example: "Search relevance improved; embeddings pipeline moved to cached KV saving 15% tpm".

5. Product telemetry highlights (4 min)
   - Trend charts: tokens per request, average latency P95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens.
   - Speaker note: Give one insight and one ask (e.g., "we recommend enabling prefix caching for high-throughput endpoints").

6. Success story / adoption win (3 min)
   - Mini case example inside the account: feature adoption, internal stakeholder quotes, or measurable KPI change.

7. Risk indicators & renewal posture (4 min)
   - Simple RAG scoring for adoption, support burden, and budget alignment.
   - Speaker note: Make a direct renewal ask if green; if amber/red, propose next steps (new pilot, technical health check, executive sponsor meeting).

8. Expansion opportunities (3 min)
   - Specific plays: embeddings for search, dedicated capacity for peak windows, observability add-on.

9. Action plan & owners (3 min)
   - 2–4 concrete actions with owners and due dates.

10. Close / decisions needed (2 min)
   - Reiterate renewal window, next meeting cadence, and immediate asks.

Enterprise (14-slide, 45–60min) flow and speaker notes:
1. Title + EBC attendees + exec sponsor (2 min)
2. Executive one-pager: strategic outcomes tied to business metrics (5 min)
   - One-line summary of impact tied to revenue, customer experience, ops efficiency.
3. Agenda & governance plan (2 min)
4. Account health deep dive: usage, cost, infra incidents, support SLAs (6 min)
5. Architecture hygiene and security posture (6 min)
   - VPC/private deployment notes, KMS/HSM status, audit logs; call out any pending remediation work.
6. Feature adoption map by org (6 min)
   - Heatmap showing teams using features; identify orphaned teams.
7. Quality and regression signals (5 min)
   - Eval results, prompt set regressions, recent model swaps and impacts.
8. Performance economics: unit cost, projected spend next 12 months (6 min)
9. Support & reliability review: SLOs, incident postmortems, outstanding bugs (5 min)
10. Expansion roadmap & pilot proposals (5 min)
11. Commercial posture: contract timeline, discounts, renewal options (5 min)
12. Risk matrix and mitigation plan (5 min)
13. Executive decisions & signposts (3 min)
14. Appendix pointers and action list (2 min)

Pre-QBR checklist (things to complete 7–10 days before):
- Confirm attendees and exec sponsor confirmed (CSM + AE responsibility).
- Pull last 12 weeks of telemetry and validate sources (owner: analytics).
- Run an automated model-eval sweep for primary endpoints and include short brief (owner: applied-ml).
- Health triage: open items filtered to top 5 impact items with remediation proposals.
- Draft a short executive one-pager for enterprise conversations.
- Prepare 2–3 measurable renewal success metrics and baseline.

Quick email templates (copy/paste):
- Invite subject: "QBR prep: [Customer] — aligning on renewal outcomes"
- Invite body: "Hi [Name], we'd like to schedule a 45-minute session to review outcomes from the last quarter, align on renewal timing, and propose a 90-day plan that unlocks additional value. Please confirm availability for [dates]. Attached is a short agenda and a one-page health snapshot. Best, [CSM]"

Renewal tracker (sample rows — paste into a sheet):
Account, ARR band, Renewal window, Renewal owner, Renewal posture (green/amber/red), Top risk, Proposed next step, Action owner, Due date
Acme Retail, $120k, 2026-03-15, Liam Chen, amber, budget cycle delayed, pilot + exec review, Marisol Gomez, 2026-02-28
FinServe Group, $850k, 2026-05-01, Aisha Patel, green, none, standard renewal, Liam Chen, 2026-04-15
MedSys Inc, $420k, 2026-04-12, Evan Brooks, red, security gaps unresolved, security remediation plan, Eng SRE, 2026-03-10

Risk signals (things that move a renewal toward amber/red):
- Consistent drop in monthly active endpoints for a key product area (>20% QoQ).
- Security/Privacy audit findings without remediation timelines.
- Multiple Sev2 incidents in the past 90 days.
- Budget holder replaced or procurement pause.
- Sustained spike in unit cost without clear ROI.

Deliverables from the QBR (example):
- Signed renewal decision or decision on timeline.
- 90-day technical health plan with owners.
- Expansion pilot charter and success metrics.
- Escalation path for exec alignment if decision postponed.

Facilitation tips:
- Keep exec slides tight: 1–2 slides, one decision ask.
- Use appendix for deep technical detail; avoid burying a renewal ask in an appendix.
- Align internally on the single narrative you want customers to walk away with (cost/save/growth).
- Have a one-page leave-behind with 3 bullets: impact to date, recommended next steps, and timeline.

Version notes and next steps:
- This draft intentionally mixes crisp executive content and more tactical slides so teams can cut or expand.
- Next: create a Google Slides master template that maps these slide numbers to a ready layout and iterate after 3 pilot QBRs.
- Assign owner for the Slides master: Marisol Gomez (action: create template v0.1 by 2026-03-05).

Appendix (supporting artifacts to attach to the deck):
- Raw telemetry export (tokens, latency, errors)
- Incident rundown csv
- Short technical runbook for on-call engineers
- Pricing and billing snapshot
- Recent model eval results

Notes to self / open items:
- Consider adding a one-slide "cost sensitivity" chart that shows impact of batching/quantization on projected spend for the account.
- Need a standard glossary for metrics (token vs request vs endpoint) linked from Confluence.
- Agree on a single source of truth for renewal posture (Jira ticket vs sheet vs Salesforce field) — propose Salesforce field as canonical.

End of draft.
